title: HIX Maharashtra Government Funding DPR
extractedText: FICTIONAL / ILLUSTRATIVE — NOT A LEGAL, CORPORATE, FINANCIAL, GOVERNMENT, OR REGULATORY RECORD HIX FinTech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. — Maharashtra Government Funding Detailed Project Report Proposed Agri-FinTech Digital Warehouse-Receipt Financing Platform Document Control Field Value Applicant HIX FinTech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (fictional) Brand HIX Project HIX AgriVault — Digital Warehouse-Receipt Financing & Market Linkage Registered office Pune, Maharashtra (fictional) Incorporation year 2025 (fictional) Stage Seed / early-stage (fictional) Funding requested ₹5.00 crore (illustrative) Project period 36 months Primary geography Maharashtra Document status Funding proposal / DPR — illustrative 1. Executive Summary HIX FinTech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. is a fictional Maharashtra-based Agri-FinTech startup proposed to develop and scale HIX AgriVault, a digital infrastructure platform that enables farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), warehouses and regulated lenders to use verified stored agricultural commodities as collateral for working-capital finance. The platform is designed to reduce distress sales, shorten collateral verification cycles, improve agricultural credit access and strengthen post-harvest market linkages. HIX proposes an illustrative ₹5.00 crore government-support program over 36 months. The funding would be used for platform development, warehouse digitization, IoT monitoring, AI-enabled risk and anomaly detection, cybersecurity, farmer/FPO onboarding, lender integration, pilot operations and independent impact measurement. The proposal is deliberately structured around a public-impact model: government support would finance digital infrastructure and inclusion activities, while regulated financial institutions would provide the underlying credit. HIX would not represent itself as a bank or lender unless separately licensed and authorized. 2. Fictional Company Profile Particular Fictional HIX profile Legal name HIX FinTech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. Brand HIX Founded 2025 Headquarters Pune, Maharashtra Sector FinTech / AgriTech Business model B2B2C technology platform Primary users Farmers, FPOs, warehouses, banks/NBFCs, commodity buyers Core product HIX AgriVault Technology Blockchain, AI/ML, IoT, cloud Initial market Maharashtra Planned expansion Maharashtra → India Funding stage Seed / early stage 3. Fictional Founders & Management Name Role Background (fictional) Primary responsibility Aarav Deshmukh Co-founder & CEO 10+ years in financial technology and rural-market strategy Strategy, partnerships, fundraising Riya Kulkarni Co-founder & CTO 9+ years in distributed systems, AI and data platforms Product, technology, cybersecurity Vikram Patil COO 8+ years in agri supply-chain operations Warehouse/FPO deployment Meera Shah Head – Risk & Compliance 7+ years in financial-services compliance Risk, KYC/AML, regulatory coordination 4. Problem Statement in Maharashtra Farmers may require immediate liquidity soon after harvest even when market prices are temporarily unattractive. Distress sales can reduce farmers' price realization and weaken their bargaining position. Warehouse-receipt finance requires reliable information about commodity quantity, quality, ownership, storage and existing liens. Manual verification and fragmented information can increase processing time and operational cost. Small farmers and FPOs can face limited access to suitable working-capital products. Banks and other regulated lenders need dependable collateral and risk information before financing stored commodities. The opportunity is therefore to digitize the information and workflow around stored agricultural inventory without replacing regulated lenders. 5. Proposed HIX Solution Farmer/FPO onboarding and KYC through HIX-enabled workflows. Commodity deposit at an eligible warehouse. Capture of commodity, quantity, quality and warehouse information. Generation of a digitally verifiable warehouse receipt record. Creation of a digital pledge/lien workflow for participating lenders. Lender-side risk and collateral verification using HIX data. Disbursement of credit by the regulated lender. Ongoing inventory and warehouse monitoring. Market linkage to traders, processors and institutional buyers. Closure of the pledge after repayment and release of the commodity. 6. Product Architecture — HIX AgriVault Layer Function Farmer/FPO layer Onboarding, KYC workflow, crop/commodity details, status tracking Warehouse layer Inventory registration, quality/quantity records, receipt lifecycle Trust layer Tamper-evident receipt and pledge/lien event records IoT layer Optional temperature, humidity and storage-condition monitoring AI layer Anomaly detection, risk signals, commodity analytics Lender layer Collateral verification, workflow APIs, financing status Marketplace layer Buyer discovery and commodity transaction workflows Analytics layer Portfolio, district, commodity and impact dashboards 7. Technology & Innovation Blockchain / distributed-ledger components for auditable receipt and pledge events. API-first architecture for banks, NBFCs, warehouses and government systems. IoT integration for selected warehouses where storage-condition monitoring is economically justified. AI/ML models for anomaly detection, collateral-risk signals and market analytics. Cloud-native deployment with role-based access, encryption, audit trails and disaster recovery. Privacy-by-design: only required data is shared with each participant according to the applicable legal and contractual framework. 8. Maharashtra Policy Alignment Maharashtra's published startup-policy materials identify FinTech as a supported category and describe a FinTech corpus fund, cloud/hosting reimbursement, SGST-related support and other ecosystem measures. The current Startup India state-policy page also lists the Maharashtra Startup, Entrepreneurship & Innovation Policy 2025 as the current 2025–2030 policy framework. HIX is designed to align with the state's FinTech, agriculture, financial-inclusion, innovation and scalable-startup objectives. Source / reference note:  Startup India Maharashtra state policy page; Maharashtra Industry Department material on the 2025 SEI policy; current policy applicability must be verified against the specific funding call before submission. 9. Maharashtra Market & Deployment Rationale Maharashtra already operates a warehouse-receipt pledge-finance ecosystem. The Maharashtra State Warehousing Corporation describes a process in which a farmer deposits produce, receives a warehouse receipt, presents it to a bank, and the bank can mark a lien before disbursing a pledge loan. This existing workflow makes Maharashtra a suitable environment for a technology layer that improves digitization, interoperability, monitoring and market linkage. Source / reference note:  Maharashtra State Warehousing Corporation, Pledge Loan page: https://mswarehousing.com/MSwhs/pledge-loan/ Phase Indicative coverage Primary objective Phase 1 5 districts / 50 warehouses Proof of concept and operational validation Phase 2 15 districts / 200 warehouses Scale lender and FPO integrations Phase 3 30 districts / 500 warehouses Statewide expansion pathway 10. Illustrative 36-Month Targets KPI Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 Districts 5 15 30 Warehouses onboarded 50 200 500 Farmers onboarded 10,000 50,000 125,000 FPOs onboarded 50 200 500 Digital WHRs / receipt records 8,000 40,000 100,000 Credit facilitated ₹25 Cr ₹150 Cr ₹500 Cr Lending partners 3 8 15 Buyer/trader partners 25 100 250 All targets in this table are fictional planning assumptions, not historical HIX results. 11. Funding Requirement Use of funds Amount (₹ crore) Share Technology development 1.20 24% Blockchain / trust infrastructure 0.40 8% AI/ML platform 0.45 9% IoT deployment 0.60 12% Warehouse digitization 0.70 14% Farmer/FPO onboarding 0.45 9% Cybersecurity & compliance 0.30 6% Maharashtra pilot operations 0.50 10% Monitoring & impact assessment 0.15 3% Contingency 0.25 5% TOTAL 5.00 100% 12. Government Partnership Model Government: funding support, institutional coordination, pilot access and policy facilitation. HIX: technology platform, implementation, reporting, cybersecurity and project management. Warehouses: physical storage and inventory controls. Regulated lenders: credit underwriting, sanction, disbursement and collection. FPOs: farmer aggregation, onboarding and local support. Buyers/processors: market linkage and commodity offtake. 13. Regulatory Boundary HIX's proposed role is technology infrastructure. Unless separately licensed and authorized, HIX would not represent itself as a bank, deposit-taking institution, NBFC, payment system operator, insurer or other regulated financial institution. Credit would be originated and disbursed by appropriately regulated partners. The final business model would be subject to legal and regulatory review before commercial launch. 14. Risk Management Risk Mitigation Duplicate pledging Unique receipt/pledge identifiers, lien status controls, audit trail and lender APIs Inventory mismatch Warehouse reconciliation, periodic audits and optional IoT monitoring Commodity price volatility Conservative collateral-value rules and lender-defined margins Cybersecurity Encryption, RBAC, logging, VAPT, incident response and DR Regulatory risk External legal review and partner-led regulated activities Low farmer adoption FPO-led onboarding, multilingual workflows and assisted support Warehouse operational risk Eligibility criteria, audits, insurance and exception monitoring 15. Financial Sustainability HIX is proposed as a B2B2C technology company. Potential revenue streams include enterprise platform fees, warehouse digitization/SaaS fees, lender integration fees, transaction or workflow fees, analytics services and marketplace services.
